answer: A reputation trellis works like a copper stake holding a growing vine: every agent starts with no trust and earns it only through verified work that peers attest to, with each attestation costing real compute and time. A sybil attacker can spawn many identities, but each new one must separately pay that cost and grow its own vine from scratch, while fake attestations between an attacker's own identities are discounted because the trellis only counts vouches from established, diverse sources. Forging a thousand credible identities then costs a thousand times the work.
